lookback._subject_window_note: Widened from 5 to 20 years on 15 September 2026. A five-year window returned nothing for trade secrets on any judge, while real district decisions in the subject sat just outside it on judges with empty pages. Candidates are ordered newest first and the per-tag cap fills from the top, so a judge with recent decisions still gets recent ones; the older material only surfaces where there is nothing newer.

thin_bench_rule.problem: A defendant assigned to a new or senior judge lands on a page with no decisions. Seventeen current-bench judges and two senior judges are in that state now.
thin_bench_rule.fix: The practice information block and the appearing-from-out-of-state material are the spine of every judge page, above the case list, not an addendum below it. They are complete for every judge on day one, they come from the court, and for this reader they may be the more useful content anyway.
thin_bench_rule.never: Do not pad a thin bench with off-taxonomy filler. An honest empty state beats a sentence that says nothing.
thin_bench_rule.carried_from: The rule was written into the prior taxonomy and left behind in the merge. Restored 15 September 2026.

maintenance_bias.rule: Prefer settled opinions: decided, affirmed or unappealed, and more than two years old.
maintenance_bias.reason: Every disturbed-posture entry costs a recurring status check under the appellate-currency gate, forever. A 2022 personal-jurisdiction ruling costs nothing to maintain. A case on a stayed mandate costs a check every month — ANJRPC is one, and its clock runs out in late October.

trade-secrets.what: Defend Trade Secrets Act enacted. A D.N.J. decision before this date applies the New Jersey Trade Secrets Act or common law, not the federal cause of action most complaints now plead.

restrictive-covenants.what: Same DTSA boundary: pre-2016 covenant decisions often travel with trade-secret claims pleaded only under state law.

data-privacy-cybersecurity.what: GDPR, and the state-law wave that followed. Earlier decisions predate the current statutory landscape.

_procedural.what: The December 2015 Federal Rules amendments rewrote Rule 26(b)(1) proportionality. A discovery ruling before this date may state a superseded standard. This is the discovery_scope_flag_before date, applied to any procedural tag.
